title: Monoidal infinity categories in the nonsymmetric Segal model
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small, and all simplicial sets considered fit in $\mathcal U'$. Use quasicategories, coherent functors and equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the simplex category $\Delta$ from [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], and cocartesian fibrations and fibers from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. As base quasicategory use the nerve $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ of the small category $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], still written $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$; its mapping spaces are the discrete sets of morphisms of $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. A morphism $[n]\to[m]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is inert if its opposite $[m]\to[n]$ is $j\mapsto a+j$ for some $a$; put $\rho_i:[n]\to[1]$ for the opposite of $j\mapsto i-1+j$, $1\leq i\leq n$.

A monoidal infinity category in the nonsymmetric model is a cocartesian fibration $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ for which the following hold. First, the transport maps along the $\rho_i$ induce equivalences $\mathcal V^\otimes_{[n]}\to(\mathcal V^\otimes_{[1]})^n$ for every $n\geq0$. Here the product is the degreewise product of quasicategories and the zeroth product is the one-point quasicategory; write $\mathcal V=\mathcal V^\otimes_{[1]}$. Second, for every $n\geq0$, every $C\in\mathcal V^\otimes_{[n]}$ and every choice of $p$-cocartesian edges $C\to C_i$ over the $\rho_i$, $1\leq i\leq n$, these edges form a relative $p$-limit: for every $m$, every $D\in\mathcal V^\otimes_{[m]}$ and every base map $\phi:[m]\to[n]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, write $\operatorname{Map}^\phi(D,C)$ for the fiber over $\phi$ of the map of mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V^\otimes}(D,C)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}([m],[n])$; then composition with the edges $C\to C_i$ induces an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}^\phi(D,C)\to\prod_{i=1}^n\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\circ\phi}(D,C_i)$, the product being degreewise and the empty product for $n=0$ being the one-point space. Cocartesian transport along the opposite of $[1]\to[n]$, $0\mapsto0$, $1\mapsto n$, is the $n$-fold tensor functor under these Segal identifications; for $n=0$ it specifies the tensor unit $\mathbf1$ up to equivalence. An edge of $\mathcal V^\otimes$ is inert if it is $p$-cocartesian and lies over an inert base map. For monoidal infinity categories $p:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ and $q:\mathcal W^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, a lax monoidal functor is a coherent functor $F:\mathcal V^\otimes\to\mathcal W^\otimes$ with $qF=p$ carrying inert edges of $\mathcal V^\otimes$ to inert edges of $\mathcal W^\otimes$; a strong monoidal functor is such an $F$ carrying all $p$-cocartesian edges to $q$-cocartesian edges.
